patterns: APPSC asks the crisis signature (high inflation, low forex, large fiscal deficit), the 1991 rescue step (IMF loan by pledging gold) and 'what was NOT done' (demonetisation, nationalisation, capital-account convertibility).
Globalisation-impact trap recurs in APPSC-G2: 'exports grew faster than imports' is the false statement; post-reform shift = enhanced global integration.
APPSC-G1 asks conceptual one-liners: SAPs reduce fiscal imbalances for long-term growth, jobless growth because reforms were confined to the formal sector, railways not much affected.
Other PSCs: year of reforms (1991, Rao/Manmohan), Chelliah = tax reforms, post-1991 changes (FDI, forex up; agriculture share not up).
App goes deeper (LERMS ratios, tariff figures, Washington Consensus, 2026 data); APPSC depth is a single conceptual fact.
